item.title: Advancing Management Research Through Theory Testing: A Special Issue of Replication and Reproducibility Studies
item.content:encoded:
William G. Obenauer, University of Maine

Robyn L. Brouer, University of South Alabama

Rachel Clapp-Smith, University of North Georgia

Ajay Rama Ponnapalli, Wayne State University

Andreas Schwab, Iowa State University

Jost Sieweke, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam

Chen Wang, Western Michigan University

Group & Organizational Management (GOM) has made an explicit commitment to publishing replication research and contributing to an ecosystem that supports replication research in the organizational sciences. By making this commitment, GOM joins journals such as Strategic Management Journal, The Leadership Quarterly, Entrepreneurship: Theory and Practice, and Journal of Management Scientific Reports in this endeavor.

As part of GOM's commitment to supporting replication research, this special issue aims to stimulate a continued stream of replication and reproducibility submissions to GOM well beyond the publication of this special issue. Focal studies (i.e., studies replicated or reproduced) are not required to have been published in GOM, but they should be of interest to GOM's audience.

Appel publié par Group & Organization Management. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Registered reports on literal replications, literal reproducibility studies, or multi-study replication designs
  • Literal replication and reproducibility studies (single-study submissions)
  • Full-length submissions using conceptual or constructive replication to advance knowledge through boundary testing or methodological improvements
  • Reproducibility studies and literal replications for benchmarking purposes within full-length submissions
  • Replication research advancing organizational sciences

Timeline

  • June 30, 2027: Initial Submissions Due

item.title: Reexamining and Replicating Foundational Studies in Entrepreneurship Research
item.content:encoded:
Karl Wennberg, Stockholm School of Economics

Jeremy C. Short, University of North Texas

Jeffrey A. Chandler, University of North Texas

Marcus Wolfe, University of North Texas

Sebastian Kruse, RWTH University

Carolin Krieweth, RWTH University

This Special Issue seeks to advance our understanding of replication in entrepreneurship research by encouraging rigorous reexaminations of foundational empirical studies. Replication is essential for cumulative theory development and for establishing confidence in empirical findings. In a dynamic field such as entrepreneurship, where institutional environments, technologies, funding regimes, and societal expectations evolve rapidly, systematic replication is particularly critical to assess whether foundational relationships reflect stable theoretical mechanisms or context-specific patterns.

Appel publié par Entrepreneurship Theory and Practice. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • The 33 most cited entrepreneurship studies (each exceeding 1,000 citations) identified as priority candidates for replication
  • Influential studies within specific BCERC research tracks highlighted as influential contributions within each track
  • Studies with credible cases for broader influence on entrepreneurship research
  • Identifying boundary conditions and contextual contingencies of established relationships
  • Clarifying inconsistencies or mixed findings in prior research
  • Refining theoretical mechanisms underlying key constructs and relationships
  • Contributing to methodological transparency, rigor, and best practices in replication research
  • Multi-study designs combining exact replication or reanalysis of original data with subsequent empirical generalization or theoretical extension

Timeline

  • December 1, 2026: Deadline for short proposal submission for paper development workshop participation (3,000-5,000 words)
  • February 1, 2027: In-person paper development workshop at University of North Texas
  • March 1, 2027: Virtual paper development workshop
  • May 1, 2027: Manuscript submission window opens
  • August 1, 2027: Manuscript submission deadline (midnight U.S. Eastern Time)
